t:
(a) Presentation Authorized.—The Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate shall make appropriate arrangements for the presentation, on behalf of the Congress, of a gold medal of appropriate design to the next of kin or personal representative of Raoul Wallenberg, in recognition of his achievements and heroic actions during the Holocaust. 
    (b) Design and Striking.—For the purpose of the presentation referred to in subsection (a), the Secretary of the Treasury shall strike a gold medal with suitable emblems, devices, and inscriptions to be determined by the Secretary.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that presenting the medal to Wallenberg's next of kin or personal representative brings an outside party into the process. They only receive the award and have no role in any federal decision. The medal's design is determined solely by the Secretary of the Treasury, and the presentation is arranged by the Speaker and the President pro tempore, all of whom are inside the federal government. There is no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Treasury shall strike a gold medal with suitable emblems, devices, and inscriptions to be determined by the Secretary

qwen_block.w: The section authorizes the presentation of a medal and specifies that the design is to be determined solely by the Secretary of the Treasury. There is no requirement for consultation with outside parties, public comment, or an advisory board with non-federal members. The actors involved (Speaker, President pro tempore, Secretary) are all inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of the Treasury shall strike a gold medal with suitable emblems, devices, and inscriptions to be determined by the Secretary.

opus.w: Every decision here is made inside the federal government. Congressional leaders arrange the presentation, and the Secretary of the Treasury alone decides the medal's design. Wallenberg's next of kin or representative only receives the medal and is not consulted on any decision. Unlike Example 10, where an advisory board set the design, no outside body is involved.
opus.s: the Secretary of the Treasury shall strike a gold medal with suitable emblems, devices, and inscriptions to be determined by the Secretary.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the presentation of a medal to an individual, but the decision-making process is entirely internal to the federal government. The design is determined solely by the Secretary of the Treasury, and the presentation is arranged by congressional leaders. There is no requirement for consultation, coordination, or input from the recipient or any other outside party before the decision is made. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Treasury shall strike a gold medal with suitable emblems, devices, and inscriptions to be determined by the Secretary.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the medal is presented "on behalf of the Congress," it involves a formal interaction with an outside party (the next of kin). However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this is a one-way presentation of an honor, not a consultation or coordination *before* a decision is made. The decision to award the medal is made by Congress (inside government), and the design is determined by the Secretary (inside government). There is no requirement for the recipient or any other outside party to participate in the decision-making process.
